response.initial_request: The tenant reports that the shower and hot water are not working. They have checked the boiler switch and report that the boiler has no power.

other_sections.Attachments: No attachments are available for this case.

events.body: Maintenance request NBL-021: shower and hot water are not working. Tenant says they checked the switch and the boiler has no power. No boiler make or model supplied; small birds are kept at the property.
Acknowledged the maintenance report and said the landlord would be contacted before next steps were confirmed. Invited the tenant to provide any further relevant details.

Tenant said there was no hot water at the taps as well as in the shower, and that the boiler had no power despite checking the switch. A household member could be at home, but the tenant asked to be contacted about arrangements; the household member does not speak English. Tenant asked if it could be addressed that day before work.

Maya said the loss of hot water would be treated as urgent and that she would contact the landlord about attendance. She said the tenant would not be charged for the reported fault, while also noting that a call-out might be chargeable if an inspection found only a switch left off. No inspection or diagnosis has taken place.

events.to: Tessa Moor (Duty Operations Lead, Northbridge Lettings)
events.body: The file was categorised as Electrical based on the tenant's report of no boiler power. The approval workflow was initiated. No inspection, diagnosis, or contractor attendance is recorded.

Reported the loss of hot water and the tenant's statement that the boiler has no power. Asked Ravi to confirm whether he would arrange attendance himself or wanted Northbridge Lettings to arrange a contractor.

events.to: Tessa Moor (Duty Operations Lead, Northbridge Lettings)
events.body: The file was moved to a landlord-managed repair route, and the approval follow-up was stopped. No contractor appointment was booked by Northbridge Lettings.
Advised that the landlord would arrange the work directly and that the tenant or household might be contacted about access. Asked the tenant to report if nobody made contact or attended.
Confirmed the landlord-managed route and asked Ravi to advise when the work was expected to be completed. Said Northbridge Lettings could arrange a contractor instead if he preferred.
Ravi said he would ask one of his own contractors to attend that day. He also asked for a building contact to message the tenant about arrangements. No contractor name or appointment time was given.
Asked whether the landlord-arranged work had been completed. Asked the tenant to say if nothing had been done or nobody had made contact.
Tenant replied: “Nothing done about it thanks.” No restoration of hot water or boiler power was reported.

Reported that the tenant said there was still no hot water and no repair had taken place. Requested an update on the contractor's timing and said Northbridge Lettings could arrange a contractor if the landlord wanted to change course.
Maya left a voicemail following up on the tenant's report of no hot water and no work completed, and asked Ravi to respond. No conversation or response was recorded.

Ravi said he believed his plumber would attend that evening. He said Northbridge Lettings could send its own contractor the following day if the plumber did not attend. No agency contractor was booked during the call.

Asked whether the plumber had attended as expected and what the outcome was. The email noted the continuing report of no hot water and asked Ravi to say if Northbridge Lettings should arrange a contractor.

Tenant said there was still no hot water and nobody had come to fix it. Tenant separately reported that the letterbox was not working and asked whether it needed to be reported separately. Maya said she would follow up; no further details or assessment of the letterbox issue were recorded.

Ravi said his plumber had attended the previous day and fixed the issue, based on a text from the plumber. No work description, report, invoice, or details of boiler or electrical checks were provided. Ravi asked to be told if the problem persisted.
Maya called to ask whether hot water had returned and left a voicemail. She said the landlord believed the issue had been resolved. No tenant confirmation was obtained during the call.
Asked the tenant to confirm whether the hot-water issue had been resolved. No reply is recorded.

events.to: Tessa Moor (Duty Operations Lead, Northbridge Lettings)
events.body: The maintenance request remains open. The landlord's update and the tenant's earlier report about the letterbox are on file.

args.reason: Waiting for Tenant: confirmation that hot water and boiler power are restored after the landlord's plumber reportedly attended on 14 May (events 18, 20). If there is no reply, phone the tenant again. If the tenant says it is still not fixed, go back to the landlord and offer an agency contractor (events 12, 13, 15). The letterbox report (event 17) is still to be followed up separately.

args.summary: The landlord says his own plumber fixed the boiler on 14 May. That is second-hand, from a text from the plumber. The tenant has not confirmed. The agency has already asked the tenant by voicemail and email on 15 May. I sent nothing new and set a follow-up for 19 May, waiting for the tenant.
facts: Tenant reported no hot water and no boiler power on 6 May (events 1, 3).
Landlord chose to use his own contractor (event 10), so the agency booked nobody (events 7, 15).
On 11 and 13 May the tenant said nothing had been done (events 12, 17).
On 15 May the landlord said his plumber attended on 14 May and fixed it, based on a text. He gave no report or invoice (event 18).
The agency left the tenant a voicemail and sent an email on 15 May asking for confirmation. No reply is recorded (events 19, 20).
The tenant also reported a broken letterbox on 13 May, which has not been assessed (event 17).
conflicts: The landlord says the fault is fixed (event 18), but the tenant's last word was that nothing had been done (events 12, 17). The tenant's account is older and the two may simply have crossed in time. The tenant has not confirmed the fix.
missing: Tenant confirmation that hot water is restored.
Any work report or invoice from the landlord's plumber.
options_rejected: Close the case: the only evidence of completion is second-hand and the tenant has not confirmed.
Escalate: no one has gone silent through repeated personal chasing and no liability is disputed. The landlord has answered each chase.
Send the tenant another message now: they were asked less than a day ago, on 15 May.
Instruct an agency contractor: the landlord is using his own and says it is fixed.
args.uncertainty: It is not known whether hot water is actually back. If the tenant says it is not, or stays silent, the next step is to phone the tenant, then ask the landlord again. Separately, the tenant said in event 4 that they would not be charged for the fault. That is not a reason to charge anyone now.

response.reason: Possible safety hazard in event 3 (no hot water); event 13 (no hot water); event 14 (no hot water); event 16 (no hot water); event 17 (no hot water).
response.how_to_fix: Do not wait on a possible hazard: act, ask or escalate instead.

args.subject: Is your hot water working again? 17 Wrenfold Quay, Larkhollow, ZZ1 1ZZ
args.body: Dear Iris, the landlord has told us his plumber attended on 14 May and fixed the hot water and boiler power at 17 Wrenfold Quay, Larkhollow, ZZ1 1ZZ. We have not heard from you since our email of 15 May. Please reply today to say whether the boiler has power and you have hot water at the taps and shower. If it is still not working, tell us and we will push for an urgent attendance, and we can send our own contractor if needed. Please also tell us the letterbox details (what is wrong with it) and we will deal with that as a separate request.

args.subject: Plumber's report needed: 17 Wrenfold Quay, Larkhollow, ZZ1 1ZZ
args.body: Dear Ravi, thank you for your update on 15 May that your plumber fixed the boiler at 17 Wrenfold Quay, Larkhollow, ZZ1 1ZZ. The tenant has not yet confirmed that hot water is back, and we have asked them to tell us. Could you send us a short note from the plumber saying what the fault was and what was done, with any invoice? If the tenant reports that the problem persists, we can arrange an agency contractor straight away if you approve.

args.summary: The landlord says his plumber fixed the boiler on 14 May, but the tenant has not confirmed. Loss of hot water is flagged as a possible hazard, so I did not wait. I asked the tenant to confirm today and to describe the letterbox fault. I asked the landlord for the plumber's report and any invoice. An earlier follow-up for 19 May is also recorded.
facts: Tenant reported no hot water and no boiler power (events 1, 3).
The landlord is using his own contractor (events 10, 15).
The tenant said nothing had been done on 11 and 13 May (events 12, 17).
On 15 May the landlord said his plumber fixed it on 14 May, based on a text, with no report (event 18).
The tenant has not replied to the 15 May voicemail and email (events 19, 20).
A letterbox fault was reported on 13 May and is unassessed (event 17).
conflicts: The landlord says it is fixed (event 18). The tenant's last word was that nothing had been done (events 12, 17). The two may simply have crossed in time.
missing: Tenant confirmation that hot water is restored.
options_rejected: Wait: blocked by the gateway as a possible hazard, and the tenant has had no hot water for about 10 days.
Close: no confirmation from the tenant and no completion evidence.
Escalate: the landlord has answered each chase, so the case is not yet stuck.
Instruct an agency contractor: no landlord approval and the landlord says it is fixed.
args.uncertainty: It is not known whether hot water is back. If the tenant says it is not, or stays silent, escalate or push for an agency contractor with landlord approval.
